ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r4.claim: Mujāhid says the People of the Book read in their scriptures that Muhammad could neither read nor write; من before كتاب is extra under negation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان أهل الكتاب يقرأون في كتبهم أن محمدا عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r5.claim: The denial of reading and writing, including the hand used to write, strengthens the proof: an unlettered man unconnected to scholars brought eloquent revelation, past history, and hidden information beyond human ability.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r5.anchor: أخذ يحقق، كونه نازلا من عند الله، بأنه ظهر عن رجل أمي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r6.claim: Most Muslims maintain that the Prophet never wrote or read from a book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r6.anchor: وأكثر المسلمين على أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يكتب قط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r7.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reportedly said the Prophet did not die until he had written; al-Naqqāsh supports the report.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r7.anchor: وروي عن الشعبي أنه قال: ما مات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، حتى كتب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r8.speaker: أبو كبشة السلولي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r8.claim: Abū Kabsha al-Sulūlī reports that the Prophet read a document belonging to ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn and explained its meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361/r8.anchor: حديث أبي كبشة السلولي: أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم، قرأ صحيفة لعيينة ابن حصن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r1.speaker: أبو ذر الهروي والباجي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r1.claim: Some, including Abū Dharr al-Harawī and al-Bājī, understand a report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim to mean the Prophet wrote directly; many local scholars fiercely condemned al-Bājī for it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r1.anchor: وقد ذهب إلى ذلك جماعة، منهم أبو ذر عبد الله بن أحمد الهروي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r2.speaker: أكثر العلماء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r2.claim: Most scholars interpret the report that he wrote as meaning he ordered the writing, as in ordinary Arabic usage where a ruler's writing to someone means he ordered a letter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r2.anchor: وتأول أكثر العلماء ما ورد من أنه كتب على أن معناه: أمر بالكتابة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r3.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r3.claim: Qatāda identifies the falsifiers who would have doubted Muhammad's revelation as the People of the Book; Mujāhid identifies them as Quraysh unbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r3.anchor: والمبطلون: أهل الكتاب، قاله قتادة أو كفار قريش، قاله مجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r4.claim: Had Muhammad read or written earlier books, opponents could allege he learned the Qur'an from them; since he did neither, their doubts have no basis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p361#2/r4.anchor: لو كان يقرأ كتبا قبل نزول القرآن عليه، أو يكتب، لحصلت الريبة للمبطلين

SAMIN-DURR:29:48/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:48/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:48/r1.claim: من كتاب is the object of تتلو, and من is extra; من قبله is either circumstantial of كتاب or attached to تتلو.
SAMIN-DURR:29:48/r1.anchor: قوله: { من كتاب }: مفعول " تتلو " و " من " زائدة. و " من قبله " حال من " كتاب " ،

SAMIN-DURR:29:48/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:48/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:48/r2.claim: Had the Prophet recited a book beforehand or been someone who writes, the falsifiers would have doubted.
SAMIN-DURR:29:48/r2.anchor: قوله " إذا لارتاب " جواب وجزاء أي: لو تلوت كتابا قبل القرآن، أو كنت ممن يكتب لارتاب المبطلون.

ZAJJAJ:v4p171/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p171/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p171/r1.claim: The Prophet had not read earlier scriptures or written; the Torah and Gospel also describe him as unlettered.
ZAJJAJ:v4p171/r1.anchor: أي ما كنت قرأت الكتب ولا كنت كاتبا، وكذلك صفة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عندهم في التوراة والإنجيل.

ZAJJAJ:v4p171/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p171/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p171/r2.claim: The people who would have doubted are identified as the Quraysh disbelievers.

ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n46/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n46/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n46/r1.claim: Yamin, literally "right hand," is a metonym for one's own hand.
ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n46/r1.anchor: Lit., "with thy right hand" - the term yamin being used here metonymically, denoting no more than one's "own hand".

ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n46/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n46/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n46/r2.claim: Because Muhammad could neither read nor write, Asad argues he could not have drawn his extensive knowledge of earlier scriptures from them; this should convince an unbiased person that it came by revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n46/r2.anchor: which - as the Qur'an points out - ought to convince any unprejudiced person that this knowledge must have come to him through divine revelation.

ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n47/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n47/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n47/r1.claim: Mubtil derives from abtala and can mean making a false or vain claim, trying to disprove or nullify something, or deeming it unfounded; the cited lexicons treat this broadly regardless of the target's truth or authenticity.
ASAD-NOTES:29:47#n47/r1.anchor: unfounded", "false", "spurious", etc.; irrespective of whether the object is true or false, authentic or spurious, valid or unfounded (Lisan al-'Arab and Taj al-'Arus).

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r1.claim: Before revelation of the Book, Muhammad could not recite any book; alternatively, reciting and writing books had not been his custom.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r1.anchor: أي وما كنت من قبل إنزالنا إليك الكتاب تقدر على أن تتلو ( من كتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r2.claim: Mentioning the right hand vividly reinforces the literal denial of writing, like saying I saw with my eye, and rules out a figurative reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r2.anchor: وذكر اليمين زيادة تصوير لما نفى عنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من الخط

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r3.claim: Had Muhammad been able or accustomed to read and write, Meccan polytheists would have suspected he copied earlier books; since he was unlettered, they had no grounds, and such a detailed book could not be learned without prolonged, visible study.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r3.anchor: لو كنت ممن يقدر على التلاوة والخط أو ممن يعتادها لأرتاب مشركو مكة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r4.claim: They are called falsifiers because they doubted and disbelieved; one explanation ties this to their doubt despite Muhammad's actual illiteracy, while another says even if he were literate their doubt would invalidate them because illiteracy is only one proof among several.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r4.anchor: ووصف مشركي مكة بالأبطال بإعتبار إرتيابهم وكفرهم وهو عليه الصلاة والسلام أمي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r5.claim: A second analysis calls them falsifiers whether or not Muhammad was unlettered: literacy would remove only one aspect of the miracle, while the remaining proofs suffice, as with doubters of non-literate prophets.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r5.anchor: وأما كونهم كذلك بالإعتبار الثاني فلأن غاية ما يلزم من عدم أميته صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r6.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r6.claim: Al-Kashf treats the conditional as a hypothetical illustration showing that the miracle is the basis of the argument; illiteracy is not the only proof, and those who deny the truth are falsifiers.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r6.anchor: وفي الكشف هذا فرض وتمثيل دلالة على أن مدار الأمر على المعجز

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid identifies the falsifiers as the polytheists of Mecca; al-Ālūsī says this is the stronger interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r7.anchor: وكون المراد بالمبطلين مشركي مكة هو المروى عن مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r8.claim: Qatāda identifies the falsifiers as the People of the Book, who would doubt because their scripture describes Muhammad as unlettered.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#2/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة : هم أهل الكتاب أي لو كنت تتلو من قبل أو تخط لأرتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r1.speaker: البغوي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r1.claim: Al-Baghawī's al-Tahdhīb chooses as the sounder view that the Prophet never learned to write after his mission either.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r1.anchor: فقيل : إنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يكن يحسن الكتاب وأختاره البغوي في التهذيب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r2.claim: Some claim that after the Qur'an was revealed, Islam spread, and the doubt had become prominent, the Prophet learned writing, his earlier inability having served the miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r2.anchor: بعضهم أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r3.speaker: ابن أبي شيبة وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v21p4#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abī Shayba and others transmit that the Prophet did not die until he had written and read.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r1.speaker: الشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbi affirmed the reported claim, saying he had heard people say it and found nothing in the verse that contradicted it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r1.anchor: للشعبي فصدقه وقال : سمعت أقواما يقولونه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r2.claim: Ibn Mājah reports from Anas that during the Night Journey the Prophet saw an inscription at Paradise's gate: charity earns tenfold and a loan eighteenfold.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r2.anchor: وروى إبن ماجه عن أنس قال : قال

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r3.claim: Although reading ability normally depends on writing, God could miraculously grant the Prophet reading without writing; alternatively, the report may omit his asking what the inscription said.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r3.anchor: والقدرة على القراءة فرع الكتابة ورد باحتمال أقدار الله تعالى إياه عليه الصلاة والسلام عليها بدونها معجزة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r4.claim: Reports in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and elsewhere about Hudaybiyya say the Prophet took the document, could not write, then wrote the treaty text; these are cited as evidence of his writing.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r4.anchor: كما ورد في صلح الحديبية فأخذ رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم الكتاب وليس يحسن يكتب فكتب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r5.speaker: أبو ذر عبد بن أحمد الهروي وأبو الفتح النيسابوري وأبو الوليد الباجي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r5.claim: These scholars held that the Prophet acquired the ability to write after his unlettered period; al-Bājī wrote a treatise, drawing on al-Sumnānī and following Ibn Munya.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r5.anchor: وممن ذهب إلى ذلك أبو ذر عبد بن أحمد الهروي وأبو الفتح النيسابوري وأبو الوليد الباجي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r6.speaker: أبو الوليد الباجي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r6.claim: When al-Bājī advanced this view, he was branded an heretic and abused publicly; he then argued it in a formal session and received support from scholars across the regions.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r6.anchor: ولما قال أبو الوليد ذلك طعن فيه ورمى بالزندقة وسب على المنابر ثم عقد له مجلس فأقام الحجة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r7.claim: The Prophet's learning to write after being unlettered would not diminish the miracle; writing without instruction would itself be another miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r7.anchor: ومعرفة الكتابة بعد أميته صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تنافي المعجزة بل هي معجزة أخرى لكونها من غير تعليم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r8.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r8.claim: Some eminent scholars rejected al-Bājī's book because of the sound report that the Muslim community is unlettered and does not write or calculate.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r8.anchor: ورد بعض الأجلة كتاب الباجي لما في الحديث الصحيح إنا أمة أمية لا نكتب ولا نحسب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r9.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r9.claim: One rebuttal interprets every hadith saying the Prophet wrote as saying that he ordered someone to write, like a ruler who writes an order for someone.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r9.anchor: بعض الأجلة كتاب الباجي لما في الحديث الصحيح إنا أمة أمية لا نكتب ولا نحسب وقال : كل ما ورد في الحديث

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r10.claim: The placement of before it ahead of nor did you write is nearly explicit that the Prophet never wrote at all; the intervening qualification does not regularly govern both sides.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r10.anchor: من قبله ) على قوله سبحانه : ( ولا تخطه ) كالصريح في أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يكتب مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r11.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r11.claim: Another eminent scholar takes before it to govern both what precedes and follows, so the verse implies that the Prophet could recite and write after revelation; otherwise it would lack benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r11.anchor: وظن بعض الأجلة رجوعه إلى ما قبله وما بعده فقال : يفهم من ذلك أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r12.claim: Even granting that syntactic reach, the claimed benefit follows only if implication is authoritative, while the scholar making the argument does not accept that principle.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r12.anchor: وأنت تعلم أنه لو سلم ما ذكره من الرجوع لا يتم أمر الإفادة إلا إذ قيل بحجية المفهوم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r13.claim: The hadith calling the community unlettered does not explicitly deny that the Prophet ever learned writing; it may describe his state at the beginning of his mission and the largely unlettered Arabs around him.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r13.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : أنا أمة أمية لا نكتب ولا نحسب ليس نصا في استمرار نفي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r14.claim: Alusi considers interpreting wrote as ordered someone to write contrary to the apparent wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r14.anchor: وأما ما ذكر من تأويل كتب بأمر بالكتابة فخلاف الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r15.speaker: القاضي عياض
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r15.claim: Al-Nawawī quotes Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ: the wording he could not write, then he wrote is nearly explicit that the Prophet wrote personally, with no need to resort to metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r15.anchor: نقلا عن القاضي عياض أن قوله في الرواية التي ذكرناها : ولا يحسن يكتب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r16.claim: Alusi notes that each side argued at length and denounced the other, then leaves the matter to God, who knows best.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r16.anchor: وقد طال كلام كل فرقة في هذه المسئلة وشنعت كل فرقة على الأخرى في هذا فالله تعالى أعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r17.speaker: بعض الكتب
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r17.claim: An unidentified book says the Prophet could not read writing directly but knew its contents when its letters announced their names to him, like the foreleg that spoke to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5/r17.anchor: ورأيت في بعض الكتب ولا أدري الآن أي كتاب هو أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لم يكن يقرأ ما يكتب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p5#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5#2/r1.claim: Alusi says the claim that the letters disclosed their names to the Prophet cannot be accepted without a sound report, which he has not found.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p5#2/r1.anchor: أن مثل هذا لا يقبل بدون خبر صحيح ولم أظفر به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r6.claim: Before revelation, Muhammad neither read nor wrote books.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r6.anchor: أي: لم تكن تقرأ ولا تكتب قبل الوحي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r7.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r7.claim: Qatada says that if Muhammad had read or written, Meccan polytheists would have doubted him and alleged he copied earlier books.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r7.anchor: لو كنت تكتب أو تقرأ الكتب قبل الوحي لشك المبطلون المشركون من أهل مكة، وقالوا: إنه يقرؤه من كتب الأولين وينسخه منها، قاله قتادة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r8.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r8.claim: Muqatil identifies the falsifiers as Jews, who would accuse Muhammad of failing the Torah’s description of an unlettered prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p249/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل: "المبطلون" هم اليهود، ومعناه: إذا لشكوا فيك واتهموك

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r5.claim: The unlettered Prophet's delivery of a book gathering noble sciences despite not reading is extraordinary evidence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r5.anchor: فإن ظهور هذا الكتاب الجامع لأنواع العلوم الشريفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r6.claim: Mentioning the right hand makes the negation vivid and rules out figurative attribution of writing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r6.anchor: وذكر اليمين زيادة تصوير للمنفي ونفي للتجوز

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r7.claim: If he had read or written, falsifiers would suspect that he learned or copied from earlier scriptures; they are so named for disbelief or doubt despite many proofs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r7.anchor: لو كنت ممن يخط ويقرأ لقالوا لعله تعلمه أو التقطه

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r8.claim: Another view says People of the Book would doubt because the Prophet's description differed from their scriptures; they would be falsifiers in actuality, not hypothetically.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:47-48/r8.anchor: وقيل لارتاب أهل الكتاب لوجدانهم نعتك على خلاف ما في كتبهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r7.claim: Before the Quran, Muhammad had never regularly read any book; the wording denies sustained reading at any time.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r7.anchor: أي تقرأ مواصلا مواظبا في وقت ما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r8.claim: Min extends the negation over both much and little of the time before the Quran’s revelation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r8.anchor: ولما كان المراد نفي التلاوة عن كثير الزمن الماضي وقليله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r9.claim: The repeated min emphasizes that Muhammad had read no book at all.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r9.anchor: وأكد استغراق الكتب فقال : { من كتاب } أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r10.claim: Muhammad did not habitually write; the verse stresses that his stronger right hand was not used to write a book.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r10.anchor: أي تجدد وتلازم خطه ؛ وصور الخط وأكده

BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r11.claim: Prior sustained reading or writing could have given falsifiers grounds for doubt, but Muhammad had never practiced it enough to gain mastery.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r11.anchor: إذ لو كان شيء من هذه المواظبة في التلاةو أو الخط

BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r12.claim: The falsifiers are those among the People of the Book and Arabs who reject revelation and accuse the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p565/r12.anchor: أي هؤلاء الذين ينكرون الوحي إليك من أهل الكتاب ومن العرب

DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r1.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet warning Muslims not to ask People of the Book: they may affirm falsehood or deny truth; if Moses were alive, he would have to follow the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تسألوا هل الكتاب عن شيء

DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says he heard that the Prophet warned against asking People of the Book, who cannot guide and have themselves gone astray.
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال: بلغني أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لا تسألوا أهل الكتاب عن شيء فإنهم لن يهدوكم

DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud advises avoiding questions to People of the Book; if unavoidable, accept what agrees with the Qur’an and leave what conflicts with it.
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: لا تسألوا أهل الكتاب عن شيء فإنهم لن يهدوكم

DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says People of the Book found in their scriptures that Muhammad would neither write with his right hand nor read a book; Quraysh would have doubted if he had done so.
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك} قال: كان أهل الكتاب يجدون في كتبهم

DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet was unable to read or write; God had revealed his description in the Torah and Gospel to learned People of the Book, with his unlettered state itself a sign of prophethood.
DURR-FULL:v6p469#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك} قال: لم يكن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ ولا يكتب

DURR-FULL:v6p470/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p470/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p470/r1.claim: Qatada says the Prophet had neither read earlier scripture nor written, and was unlettered; the Prophet himself is the clear sign, among the learned People of the Book.
DURR-FULL:v6p470/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك} قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يقرأ كتابا قبله

DURR-FULL:v6p470/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p470/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v6p470/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the Prophet neither read nor wrote, as the Torah and Gospel described him as unlettered; his recognizable description is a clear sign, and those who deny it are unjust.
DURR-FULL:v6p470/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك في الآية قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يقرأ ولا يكتب وكذلك جعل نعته في التوراة والإنجيل

DURR-FULL:v6p470/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p470/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p470/r4.claim: Ibn Masud says the Messenger of God neither read nor wrote.
DURR-FULL:v6p470/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه في قوله {وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب} قال: لم يكن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ ولا يكتب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r1.claim: Mujahid says the people of the Book found in their scriptures that Muhammad neither wrote with his right hand nor read a book, and that this verse was then revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد وما كنت تتلوا من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك اذا قال كان اهل الكتاب يجدون في كتبهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r2.claim: Qatada says the Prophet did not read a prior book or write it with his right hand; an ummī is one who does not write.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وما كنت تتلوا من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet was ummī and could neither read nor write.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ولا تخطه بيمينك قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اميا لا يقرا ولا يكتب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm defines an ummī as someone who can read but cannot write.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r4.anchor: عن ابراهيم قال : الامي : يقرا ولا يكتب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies the deniers who would have doubted as Quraysh.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3071/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : اذا لارتاب المبطلون قريش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r4.claim: The Prophet’s known illiteracy is powerful evidence that revelation came from God; the Qur’an elsewhere also invokes his prior lack of knowledge of scripture and his lifetime among his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r4.anchor: هذا استدلال بصفة الأمية المعروف بها الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ودلالتها على أنه موحى إليه من الله أعظم دلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r5.claim: He had not read any book before the Qur’an, preventing anyone from claiming it was drawn from books he had previously recited.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r5.anchor: أنك لم تكن تقرأ كتابا حتى يقول أحد : هذا القرآن الذي جاء به هو مما كان يتلوه من قبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r6.claim: The verse also denies writing any book, even without reciting one, excluding both routes of learning and fully establishing illiteracy; a memorizer who cannot write and a copyist who lacks learned knowledge are not considered illiterate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r6.anchor: فالمقصود نفي حالتي التعلم ، وهما التعلم بالقراءة والتعلم بالكتابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r7.claim: Idhan is the response and consequence of an implicit law condition inferred from the Prophet’s not reading or writing: had he done either before, falsifiers would have doubted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p9/r7.anchor: جواب وجزاء لشرط مقدر ب ( لو ) لأنه مفروض دل عليه قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r1.speaker: المرزوقي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r1.claim: Al-Marzūqī reads the second hemistich of Qurayẓ al-ʿAnbarī’s poem as answering an imagined question about what Banū Māzin would do if the camels were raided.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r1.anchor: قال المرزوقي في ( شرح الحماسة ) : ( إذن ) هو أنه أخرج البيت الثاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r2.claim: The author also allows “then they would have supported me” to answer the implicit law condition, as if it were a second answer; similarly, “if free, I would condemn slaves’ deeds; then I would admire free men’s deeds.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أيضا : إذن لقام ، جواب ( لو ) كأنه أجيب بجوابين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r3.claim: Irtiyāb means the occurrence of doubt in the mind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r3.anchor: والارتياب : حصول الريب في النفس وهو الشك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r4.claim: Prior reading or writing could have raised a suspicion that the Qur’an came from earlier books or material he had copied; this would invite preliminary doubt, not justify certainty of denial, since its style and meaning refute the suspicion after reflection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r4.anchor: لو كان ذلك واقعا لاحتمل عندهم أن يكون القرآن من جنس ما كان يتلوه من قبل من كتب سالفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r5.claim: “With your right hand” emphasizes writing, since writing is done by the right hand, like the Qur’an’s “no bird that flies with its wings” at 6:38.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r5.anchor: وتقييد تخطه } بقيد { بيمينك } للتأكيد لأن الخط لا يكون إلا باليمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r6.claim: They are called people of falsehood because their denial is baseless; the description signals that they are deeply immersed in falsehood, paralleling “the disbelievers” in the prior verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p10/r6.anchor: ووصف المكذبين بالمبطلين منظور فيه لحالهم في الواقع لأنهم كذبوا مع انتفاء شبهة الكذب

BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r1.claim: Before the Qur'an was revealed, Muhammad did not customarily recite any revealed book or write one.
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r1.anchor: {ولا تخطه} ولا أن تكتب كتابا من الكتب

BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r2.claim: Khaṭṭ means drawing something long and is used for writing; the right hand is mentioned because people usually write with it.
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r2.anchor: والخط كالمد ويقال لما له طول ويعبر عن الكتابة بالخط

BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r3.claim: Mention of the right hand reflects the custom of right-handed writing, not an implication that left-handed writing is impossible; it is exceptionally rare.
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r3.anchor: يعني ذكر اليمين لكون الكتابة غالبا باليمين لا أنه لا يخط بيمينه ويخط بشماله

BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r4.speaker: الشيعة
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r4.claim: The Shia say Muhammad could write before revelation but was forbidden by revelation; they read the phrase as a prohibition and say it does not deny earlier writing.
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r4.anchor: قال الشيعة : إنه عليه السلام كان يحسن الخط قبل الوحي ثم نهي عنه بالوحى

BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r5.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r5.claim: Kashf al-Asrar notes a rare reading with fatḥa on ṭāʾ as a prohibition, but says the correct view is that the Prophet did not write.
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r5.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : قرىء ولا تخطه بالفتح على النهي وهو شاذ والصحيح أنه لم يكن يكتب

BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r6.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r6.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima rejects the Shia argument: if the phrase were prohibitive, ṭāʾ should be subjunctive, or the verb would be intensified as لا تخططه.
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r6.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" : قول الشيعة مردود لأن لا تخطه لو كان نهيا لكان ينصب الطاء

BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r7.claim: Had Muhammad been accustomed to reciting and writing, falsifiers could suspect he learned or copied the Qur'an from earlier books; since he was not, there is no basis for doubt.
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r7.anchor: وقالوا : لعله تعلمه أو التقته من كتب الأوائل وحيث لم تكن كذلك لم يبق في شأنك منشأ ريب أصلا

BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r9.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r9.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes rayb as a suspicion exposed as false, irāba as one not dispelled, and irtiyāb as similar to irāba; he cites the believers' lack of doubt in 74:31.
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r9.anchor: قال في "المختار" : الريب الشك. قال الراغب : الريب أن

BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r10.claim: A mubṭil brings falsehood, the opposite of a muḥiqq, who brings truth.
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r10.anchor: والمبطل من يأتي بالباطل وهو نقيض المحق وهو من يأتي بالحق

BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r11.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r11.claim: Al-Mufradat says ibṭāl means destroying or removing something, and can describe someone whose assertion has no reality; 8:8 speaks of establishing truth and nullifying falsehood.
BURSEVI:v6p347#2/r11.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : الإبطال يقال في إفساد الشيء وإزالته حقا كان الشيء أو باطلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r5.claim: The Qur’an’s inimitable length and reports of the unseen, delivered by an unlettered Prophet who neither read nor wrote, demonstrate its divine origin; literacy would have given deniers grounds for doubt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r5.anchor: مما يقوي نزول هذا القرآن من عند الله أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم جاء به في غاية الإعجاز والطول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the People of the Book found in their scriptures that Muhammad would neither write nor read a book, and this verse was revealed on that account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كان أهل الكتاب يجدون في كتبهم أن محمدا لا يخط ولا يقرأ كتابا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r7.speaker: الشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, as cited by al-Naqqāsh, reportedly said the Prophet had written before his death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r7.anchor: وذكر النقاش في تفسير هذه الآية عن الشعبي أنه قال: ما مات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى كتب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r8.speaker: أبو كبشة السلولي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r8.claim: A report traced to Abū Kabsha al-Sulūlī says the Prophet read ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn’s document and told him its meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p321#2/r8.anchor: وأسند أيضا حديثا إلى أبي كبشة السلولي مضمنه أنه عليه السلام قرأ صحيفة لعيينة بن حصن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p322/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p322/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p322/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the reports that the Prophet wrote or read a document weak, including al-Bājī’s position.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p322/r1.anchor: قال الفقيه الإمام القاضي: وهذا كله ضعيف، وقول الباجي رحمه الله منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p322/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p322/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p322/r7.claim: Qatāda identifies the “falsifiers” as the Jews.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda takes the phrase to mean that the Prophet had not read a book before the Qurʾān; min is extra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة مجازة ما كنت تقرأ قبله كتابا ومن زائدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r2.claim: The pronoun in before it refers to the Qurʾān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r2.anchor: فأما الهاء في قبله فهي عائدة إلى القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r3.claim: Before revelation Muhammad neither read nor wrote; the Torah and Gospel likewise describe him as unlettered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r3.anchor: والمعنى ما كنت قارئا قبل الوحي ولا كاتبا وهكذا كانت صفته في التوراة والإنجيل أنه أمي لا يقرأ ولا يكتب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r4.claim: His prior illiteracy shows that what he brought came from God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r4.anchor: وهذا يدل على ان الذي جاء به من عند الله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r5.claim: Had he been able to read and write, Jews would have doubted him and said that his condition contradicted their scripture.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r5.anchor: لو كنت قارئا كاتبا لشك اليهود فيك ولقالوا ليست هذه صفته في كتابنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r6.claim: Al-mubṭilūn are people who bring falsehood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r6.anchor: والمبطلون الذين يأتون بالباطل وفيهم ها هنا قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r7.claim: One view identifies the people called al-mubṭilūn here as the Quraysh disbelievers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r7.anchor: وفيهم ها هنا قولان أحدهما كفار قريش قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p277#2/r8.claim: A second view identifies al-mubṭilūn as the Jewish disbelievers.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r6.claim: Before the Quran, Muhammad had lived among his people for a long time without reading books or knowing how to write; everyone knew him as unlettered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r6.anchor: أي: قد لبثت في قومك -يا محمد -ومن قبل أن تأتي بهذا القرآن عمرا لا تقرأ كتابا ولا تحسن الكتابة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r7.claim: The Prophet’s unlettered status was also stated in earlier scriptures, including the Torah and Gospel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r7.anchor: الذين يتبعون الرسول النبي الأمي الذي يجدونه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r8.claim: Muhammad remained unable to write even a line or letter by hand; scribes wrote revelation and letters to the regions for him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r8.anchor: لا يحسن الكتابة ولا يخط سطرا ولا حرفا بيده، بل كان له كتاب يكتبون بين يديه الوحي والرسائل إلى الأقاليم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects the claim by later jurists, including al-Baji, that Muhammad himself wrote the Hudaybiyya document; the Bukhari wording that he took and wrote is read alongside the other version, that he ordered it written.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r9.anchor: فإنما حمله على ذلك رواية في صحيح البخاري: "ثم أخذ فكتب": وهذه محمولة على الرواية الأخرى: "ثم أمر فكتب".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir says jurists in East and West strongly condemned those who followed al-Baji and disassociated from that view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r10.anchor: ولهذا اشتد النكير بين فقهاء المغرب والمشرق على من قال بقول الباجي، وتبرؤوا منه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir suggests al-Baji may have meant that Muhammad wrote the document miraculously, not that he knew writing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r11.anchor: إنما أراد الرجل -أعني الباجي، فيما يظهر عنه -أنه كتب ذلك على وجه المعجزة، لا أنه كان يحسن الكتابة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r12.claim: The Prophet’s report that the Dajjal has the word kafir written between his eyes, also recited as three letters, illustrates writing as a miracle rather than literacy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r12.anchor: كما قال، عليه الصلاة والسلام (2) إخبارا عن الدجال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r13.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r13.claim: A report claiming that the Prophet learned writing before he died is weak and has no basis, according to Ibn Kathir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r13.anchor: أنه لم يمت، عليه السلام (4) حتى تعلم الكتابة، فضعيف لا أصل له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r14.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r14.claim: The two negations reinforce the denial that Muhammad had previously read a book or written with his right hand; the latter wording is a common-case expression, like the bird flying with its wings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p285/r14.anchor: لتأكيد النفي، {ولا تخطه بيمينك} تأكيد أيضا، وخرج مخرج الغالب،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p286/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p286/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p286/r1.claim: Had Muhammad known reading and writing, ignorant people could have suspected that he learned the Quran from earlier books of the prophets.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p286/r1.anchor: لو كنت تحسنها (5) لارتاب بعض الجهلة من الناس فيقول: إنما تعلم هذا من كتب قبله مأثورة عن الأنبياء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p286/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p286/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p286/r2.claim: Although they knew Muhammad was unlettered, opponents still called the Quran ancient tales written down and dictated morning and evening; God replies that it was sent by the Knower of the heavens’ and earth’s secret.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p286/r2.anchor: أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna interprets taghannī as finding sufficiency in the Quran; Abu Ubayd and others followed him if this means dispensing with worldly things.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة: إن المراد بالتغني: يستغني به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects worldly self-sufficiency as contrary to the hadith’s apparent intent, preferring audible recitation, beautification, and plaintive reading, as some transmitters explained it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.anchor: فخلاف الظاهر من مراد الحديث؛ لأنه قد فسره بعض رواته بالجهر، وهو تحسين القراءة والتحزين بها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.claim: Shafi‘i rejects the sufficiency interpretation: that meaning would call for yataghana bihi; instead the Quran is recited with sorrow and melody.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.anchor: فقال لي الشافعي: ليس هو هكذا، ولو كان هكذا لكان يتغانى به، وإنما هو يتحزن ويترنم به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.speaker: ابن وهب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.claim: Ibn Wahb says taghannī means singing or chanting melodiously; al-Muzani and al-Rabi‘ likewise report this interpretation from Shafi‘i.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.anchor: وسمعت ابن وهب يقول: يترنم به، وهكذا نقل المزني والربيع عن الشافعي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir finds Bukhari’s use of 29:51 as a chapter heading ill-fitting: its context answers a demand for prophetic signs, whereas the chapter concerns Quranic melody or sufficiency.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.anchor: فعلى كل تقدير، تصدير الباب بهذه الآية الكريمة فيه نظر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.claim: The Prophet had read no earlier scripture and written none by hand, so would-be falsifiers would have had grounds for doubt; this supports the Quran’s authenticity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.anchor: أي: وقد جئت فيه بخبر الأولين والآخرين فأين هذا من التغني بالقرآن وهو تحسين الصوت به

JISHUMI:v8p5577/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5577/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5577/r2.claim: “Nor do you write it” is indicative, coordinated with the preceding negation; a prohibition would be subjunctive.
JISHUMI:v8p5577/r2.anchor: (ولا تخطه) رفع؛ لأنه نفي معطوف على نفي وهو قوله: (ما كنت تتلو) ولو كان نهيا لكان نصبا

JISHUMI:v8p5577/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5577/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5577/r3.claim: If the Prophet wrote while claiming not to, that would create greater suspicion.
JISHUMI:v8p5577/r3.anchor: ولأنه لو كان يكتبه وأظهر أنه لا يكتبه لكانت الشبهة أعظم.

JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r13.claim: God kept the Prophet from reading and writing to prevent suspicion and rejection; as caller, lawgiver, and explainer he needed to be readily accepted.
JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r13.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وما كنت تتلو) الآيات، على أنه جنب رسوله كل ما ينفي عنه، وأنه إنما نزهه من القراءة والخط؛ لئلا يرتاب أحد، وينفر،

JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r14.claim: If protection from reading and writing is needed to avoid repelling people, avoiding major sins and fisq is even more necessary.
JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r14.anchor: وإنما يجب تنزيهه من المنفرات؛ لأنه بعث داعيا وشارعا ومبينا، فوجب أن يكون على صفة يكون الناس إلى القبول منه أقرب،

JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r15.claim: Doubt is a human act; if God created it, it would persist and not vary with the Prophet's literacy, refuting the Mujbira on creation and capacity.
JISHUMI:v8p5579#2/r15.anchor: وتدل أن الارتياب فعل العبد؛ إذ لو كان خلقا له تعالى لوقف عليه ولما اختلف بكون النبي كاتبا وقارئا، فيبطل قول المجبرة في المخلوق، وكذلك في الاستطاعة.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r1.claim: Muhammad was unlettered: no one had ever known him to recite a book or write one.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r1.anchor: وأنت أمي ما عرفك أحد قط بتلاوة كتاب ولا خط

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r2.claim: If he had read or written, the People of the Book could doubt him, saying he did not match their description of an unlettered prophet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r2.anchor: من أهل الكتاب وقالوا : الذي نجده في كتبنا أمي لا يكتب ولا يقرأ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, Meccan polytheists might suspect that Muhammad learned the Qur’an or wrote it himself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r3.anchor: أو لارتاب مشركو مكة وقالوا : لعله تعلمه أو كتبه بيده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r4.claim: They are called falsifiers because they disbelieved despite his illiteracy, which leaves no ground for suspicion; literacy would invite stronger doubts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r4.anchor: سماهم مبطلين لأنهم كفروا به وهو أمي بعيد من الريب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r5.claim: Other prophets were not unlettered, yet belief in them was required because God confirmed them through miracles; even supposing Muhammad literate, his opponents should believe by the same proof, especially since the Qur’an is miraculous while earlier scriptures are not.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r5.anchor: سائر الأنبياء عليهم السلام لم يكونوا أميين ، ووجب الإيمان بهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r6.claim: Mentioning the right hand, the instrument of writing, makes the denial that he wrote more vivid, as it would strengthen an affirmation that he wrote a book.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p462#2/r6.anchor: ذكر اليمين وهي الجارحة التي يزاول بها الخط : زيادة تصوير لما نفى عنه من كونه كاتبا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r1.claim: One account says Muhammad had not read any revealed book before the Qur’an or written one with his right hand, so opponents could not claim he learned revelation’s contents from such a book.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r1.anchor: حتى يشكوا في إخبارك عنه إنه من وحي الله سبحانه إليك وهو معنى قول يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r2.claim: Mujahid says the People of the Book had found in their scriptures that Muhammad would neither write with his right hand nor read a book; the verse came to establish his prophethood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r2.anchor: أنه كان أهل الكتاب يجدونه في كتبهم أن محمدا لا يخط بيمينه ولا يقرأ كتابا فنزل ذلك فيهم ليدلهم على صحة نبوته

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the falsifiers who would doubt as the Quraysh polytheists.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r3.anchor: أحدها : أنهم مشركو قريش , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r4.claim: Qatada says Arab polytheists would have claimed Muhammad learned from someone else if he had read.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r4.anchor: الثاني : مشركو العرب أن يقولوا لو كان يقرأ قد تعلمه من غيره , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r5.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the falsifiers as Jews who denied the message.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p287/r5.anchor: الثالث : أنهم المكذبون من اليهود , قاله السدي

MUJAHID:v2p497/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p497/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p497/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the skeptics who would have doubted as Quraysh.
MUJAHID:v2p497/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ إذا لارتاب المبطلون ﴾ يعني قريشا

MUQATIL:29:48-49/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r1.claim: Muhammad had not read any book before the Qur'an; if he had, Jews could say he composed the Qur'an himself.
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r1.anchor: وما كنت } يا محمد { تتلو } يعنى تقرأ { من قبله } يعنى من قبل القرآن

MUQATIL:29:48-49/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r2.claim: Muhammad had not written with his right hand; otherwise falsifiers could claim he wrote the revelation himself.
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r2.anchor: من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك } فلو كنت يا محمد تتلوا القرآن أو تخطه، لقالت اليهود،

MUQATIL:29:48-49/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r3.claim: Irtāba means to doubt, and the falsifiers are lying unbelievers among the Jews.
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r3.anchor: إذا لارتاب } يقول: وإذا لشك { المبطلون } [آية: 48] يعنى الكاذبين، يعنى كفار اليهود

MUQATIL:29:48-49/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r4.claim: The Torah describes Muhammad as unlettered, unable to read or write.
MUQATIL:29:48-49/r4.anchor: إن الذى نجد فى التوراة نعته، هو أمى لا يقرأ الكتاب ولا يخطه بيده.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r1.claim: Before the Quran, the Prophet neither read a book nor wrote; right hand is specified because writing is usually done with it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r1.anchor: خص اليمين لأن الكتابة عالبا تكون باليمين أى ما كنت قرأت كتابا من الكتب ولا كنت كاتبا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r2.claim: Idhan means if that were so and refers to reading or writing before revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r2.anchor: أى لو كان شيء من ذلك أى من التلاوة ومن الخط

NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r3.claim: The falsifiers may be People of the Book, who would doubt that he was the unlettered prophet in their scriptures, or Meccan polytheists, who might allege he learned or wrote the Quran.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r3.anchor: من أهل الكتاب وقالوا الذى نجد نعته فى كتبنا امى لا يكتب ولا يقرأ وليس به أو لارتاب مشركو مكة وقالوا لعله تعلمه أو كتبه بيده

NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r4.claim: They are called falsifiers because they deny his prophethood.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r5.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r5.claim: Mujahid and al-Shabi say the Prophet did not die until he had written and read.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p261#4/r5.anchor: وعن مجاهد والشعبى ما مات النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى كتب وقرأ

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r1.claim: The pronoun ‘before it’ refers to the Quran: Muhammad did not read an earlier book or associate with the People of the Book; the Quran came with inimitability and knowledge of the unseen.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r1.anchor: الضمير في { قبله } عائد إلى الكتاب وهو القرآن المنزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أي وما كنت يا محمد تقرأ قبله، ولا تختلف إلى أهل الكتاب،

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r2.claim: Had Muhammad read or written books, falsifiers—especially the People of the Book—could have claimed their scriptures predicted an unlettered man who neither writes nor reads, not him.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r2.anchor: فلو كنت ممن يقرأ كتابا، ويخط حروفا { لارتاب المبطلون } أي من أهل الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r3.claim: Mujahid says the People of the Book found in their scriptures that Muhammad neither wrote nor read, and the verse was revealed in response.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان أهل الكتاب يجدون في كتبهم أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يخط ولا يقرأ فنزلت هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas calls this evidence of prophethood to Quraysh: Muhammad could not read or write, did not mix with the People of the Book in Mecca, yet brought accounts of earlier prophets and peoples.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r4.anchor: قال النحاس: دليلا على نبوته لقريش لأنه لا يقرأ ولا يكتب ولا يخالط أهل الكتاب ولم يكن بمكة أهل الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r5.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r5.claim: Al-Nuqqash cites al-Shabi as saying the Prophet had learned to write by the time he died; he also cites a report that the Prophet read Uyayna ibn Hisn’s letter and explained it.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r5.anchor: ذكر النقاش في تفسير هذه الآية عن الشعبي أنه قال: ما مات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى كتب.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls these reports weak, including al-Baji’s position.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا كله ضعيف، وقول الباجي رحمه الله منه.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r7.speaker: البراء
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r7.claim: In al-Bara’s Hudaybiyya report, the Prophet asked Ali to write the treaty; when Quraysh objected to ‘Messenger of God,’ he erased those words and wrote ‘son of Abd Allah.’
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r7.anchor: من حديث البراء في صلح الحديبية

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r8.speaker: البخاري
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r8.claim: Al-Bukhari’s account more explicitly says the Prophet took the document and wrote; another route adds that he did not know how to write.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r8.anchor: وقد رواه البخاري بأظهر من هذا. فقال: فأخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الكتاب فكتب. وزاد في طريق أخرى: ولا يحسن أن يكتب.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r9.speaker: السمناني
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r9.claim: Al-Sumnani, Abu Dharr, and al-Baji accept the apparent report that the Prophet wrote with his own hand, but say this does not undermine his being unlettered or conflict with the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48/r9.anchor: فقال جماعة، بجواز هذا الظاهر عليه وأنه كتب بيده، منهم السمناني وأبو ذر والباجي، ورأوا أن ذلك غير قادح في كونه أميا،

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r1.speaker: السمناني
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r1.claim: Those accepting the apparent report cite the hadith that the Muslim community is unlettered and does not write or calculate, and consider the act an added miracle.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r1.anchor: إنا أمة أمية لا نكتب ولا نحسب

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r2.speaker: السمناني
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r2.claim: Their explanation is that God caused the Prophet’s hand and pen to make understood marks without his learning writing; they compare this to his knowledge without learning.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه كتب من غير تعلم لكتابة، ولا تعاط لأسبابها، وإنما أجرى الله تعالى على يده وقلمه حركات

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r3.speaker: أبو العباس أحمد بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Umar condemns accusing proponents of unbelief: the issue rests on sound solitary reports and apparent readings, is not definitive, and is not impossible by reason or revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r3.anchor: قال شيخنا أبو العباس أحمد بن عمر: وقد أنكر هذا كثير من متفقهة الأندلس وغيرهم، وشددوا النكير فيه، ونسبوا قائله إلى الكفر،

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r4.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r4.claim: A later scholar argues that the Prophet’s writing would contradict the miracle of being unlettered; miracles cannot cancel one another, so ‘he wrote’ means he directed a scribe.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r4.anchor: قال بعض المتأخرين من قال هي آية خارقة، فيقال له: كانت تكون آية لا تنكر

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r5.claim: The account notes that twenty-six scribes wrote revelation in the Prophet’s presence.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r5.anchor: وكان من كتبة الوحي بين يديه صلى الله عليه وسلم ستة وعشرون كاتبا.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r6.speaker: معاوية
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r6.claim: Qadi Iyad cites Muawiya’s report that he wrote before the Prophet, who instructed him in the form of letters and in writing the divine names.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#2/r6.anchor: عن معاوية أنه كان يكتب بين يدي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال له

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r1.speaker: القاضي عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r1.claim: Qadi Iyad says that although the report of the Prophet writing is not sound, it is possible that he was given knowledge of writing while being prevented from reading and writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r1.anchor: قال القاضي: وهذا وإن لم تصح الرواية أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كتب فلا يبعد أن يرزق علم هذا،

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the correct view is that the Prophet wrote no letter and read or spelled nothing; he instructed a scribe to write for him.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r2.anchor: قلت: هذا هو الصحيح في الباب أنه ما كتب ولا حرفا واحدا، وإنما أمر من يكتب وكذلك ما قرأ ولا تهجى.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r3.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r3.claim: An objection cites the Prophet spelling the letters in the word kafir, said to appear between the Dajjal’s eyes.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r3.anchor: فقد تهجى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين ذكر الدجال فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi answers from Hudhayfa’s report that every believer, literate or not, can read the word on the Dajjal; this does not contradict the Prophet’s illiteracy.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r4.anchor: فالجواب ما نص عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث حذيفة،

QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r5.speaker: حذيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r5.claim: Hudhayfa’s hadith explicitly says every believer can read the Dajjal’s mark, whether literate or unlettered.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:48#3/r5.anchor: ففي حديث حذيفة: «يقرؤه كل مؤمن كاتب وغير كاتب» فقد نص في ذلك على غير الكتاب ممن يكون أميا.

RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r1.claim: This is a further step in the argument: after the earlier analogy, al-Razi identifies the shared basis as the miracle proving that earlier books were revealed and that this Qur’an is revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r1.anchor: ذكر أولا التمثيل بقوله : { وكذلك أنزلنا إليك } ( العنكبوت : 47 ) ثم ذكر الجامع وهو المعجزة

RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r2.claim: That the Qur’an came through someone who neither wrote nor read is itself a miracle and establishes its revealed origin.
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r2.anchor: ما علم كون تلك الكتب منزلة إلا بالمعجزة ، وهذا القرآن ممن لم يكتب ولم يقرأ عين المعجزة

RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r3.claim: Even a literate Prophet could not have authored this inimitable discourse, but literacy would give opponents some ground for doubt; his actual condition leaves them no ground.
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r3.anchor: فإن جميع كتبة الأرض وقرائها لا يقدرون عليه ، لكن على ذلك التقدير يكون للمبطل وجه ارتياب

RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r4.claim: Al-Razi reads “from someone like him” in the challenge as meaning someone like Muhammad, connecting the challenge to the Prophet’s inability to read or write.
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r4.anchor: أي من مثل محمد عليه السلام وكقوله

RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r5.claim: He also invokes the opening declaration that the Book has no doubt.
RAZI-FULL:v25p68/r5.anchor: وكقوله : { الم * ذالك الكتاب لا ريب فيه } ( البقرة : 1 / 2 )

STUDYQURAN:29:48/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r1.claim: The verse affirms a fundamental belief shared by Islamic schools: the Prophet did not author the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r1.anchor: the Prophet had no part in authoring the Quran, one of the fundamental beliefs of all schools of Islamic thought

STUDYQURAN:29:48/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r2.claim: The Prophet had lived among his people for years without reciting another book or claiming to compose one; 7:157 calls him unlettered or unschooled.

STUDYQURAN:29:48/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r3.claim: Verses 26:224–27 and 36:69 also reject that the Prophet was a poet.
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r3.anchor: Both 26:224–27 and 36:69 also reject the idea that the Prophet was a poet

STUDYQURAN:29:48/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r4.claim: His lack of recitation or composition meant false claimants had less reason to doubt revelation's origin.
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r4.anchor: had the Prophet engaged in recitation and composition, those who make false claims

STUDYQURAN:29:48/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r5.speaker: Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r5.claim: The false claimants are understood as either the Quraysh or opposing People of the Book.
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r5.anchor: meaning either the Quraysh (Ṭ, Z) or those among the People of the Book who opposed him (Z)

STUDYQURAN:29:48/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r6.claim: The charge that the Quran was written down and recited to Muhammad is illustrated at 25:5 and echoed at 6:25; 8:31; 16:24; 23:83; 27:68; 46:17; 68:15; and 83:13.
STUDYQURAN:29:48/r6.anchor: “They are fables of those of old which he has had written down

TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r1.claim: Before revelation, Muḥammad neither read a book nor wrote with his right hand; had he done so, those rejecting the message would have doubted his claim.
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r1.anchor: ولو كنت من قبل أن يوحى إليك تقرأ الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet was unlettered and neither read anything nor wrote.
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله " {وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك

TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet had not read a prior book or written with his right hand; an ummī is one who does not write.
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله " {وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب

TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid says the People of the Book found in their scriptures that the Prophet would neither write nor read a book.
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب

TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r5.claim: The falsifiers would have alleged that Muḥammad learned the Qurʾān from books, or that it was rhymed soothsaying and tales of the ancients.
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r5.anchor: القائلون: إنه سجع وكهانة، وإنه أساطير الأولين

TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r6.claim: Qatāda says they would have claimed Muḥammad learned and wrote the material himself.

TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid identifies the falsifiers in this clause as Quraysh.
TAB-FULL:v18p424#2/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله " {إذا لارتاب المبطلون}

SULAMI:v2p118#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p118#2/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v2p118#2/r1.claim: Love and divine election erased the Prophet’s customary forms and traces of nature; thus, when revelation first addressed him, it found him free of otherness. He replied that he could not read, then became at ease with the command to read in his Lord’s name (96:1).
SULAMI:v2p118#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخراز في هذه الآية : ابيدت عنه الرسوم وأشكال الطبائع لما فيه من تدبير المحبة

TABATABAI:29:46-48/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:46-48/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:46-48/r9.claim: Tilāwa means reading, whether from memory or from a written text; context indicates reading from a book here.
TABATABAI:29:46-48/r9.anchor: التلاوة هي القراءة سواء كانت عن حفظ أو عن كتاب مخطوط

TABATABAI:29:46-48/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:46-48/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:46-48/r10.claim: Khaṭṭ means writing; mubṭilūn are those who bring falsehood or, more fittingly here, claim that truth is false.
TABATABAI:29:46-48/r10.anchor: والخط الكتابة، والمبطلون جمع مبطل وهو الذي يأتي بالباطل من القول

TABATABAI:29:48/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:48/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:48/r1.claim: The apparent sense denies a habitual practice of reading or writing, rather than ability; that better fits the argument for the Qur’an’s truth and divine origin.
TABATABAI:29:48/r1.anchor: والوجه الأول أنسب بالنسبة إلى سياق الحجة وقد أقامها

TABATABAI:29:48/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:48/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:48/r2.claim: The lifetime spent among his people before revelation supports the reading that Muḥammad had no established habit of reading or writing.
TABATABAI:29:48/r2.anchor: فقد لبثت فيكم عمرا من قبله

TABATABAI:29:48/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:48/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:48/r3.claim: An alternative says the verse denies that Muḥammad was capable of reading and writing; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the habitual-practice reading as better suited to the argument.
TABATABAI:29:48/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد به نفي القدرة أي ما كنت تقدر أن تتلو وتخط من قبله

TABATABAI:29:48/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:48/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:48/r4.claim: Adding “with your right hand” is illustrative emphasis, like saying “I saw it with my eyes.”
TABATABAI:29:48/r4.anchor: وتقييد قوله { ولا تخطه } بقوله { بيمينك } نوع من التمثيل يفيد التأكيد

TABATABAI:29:48/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:48/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:48/r5.claim: Before the Qur’an, Muḥammad did not customarily read books or write; he was unlettered, so falsifiers had no basis to suspect he composed it from earlier scriptures or stories.
TABATABAI:29:48/r5.anchor: لم يبق محل ريب لهم في أمر القرآن النازل إليك أنه كلام الله تعالى وليس تلفيقا

TABRISI:29:46-50/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:46-50/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:46-50/r8.claim: Before revelation, Muhammad neither read nor wrote a book; he did not know how to read before receiving the Qurʾān.
TABRISI:29:46-50/r8.anchor: وما كنت يا محمد تقرأ قبل القرآن كتابا

TABRISI:29:46-50/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:46-50/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:46-50/r9.claim: Had he read or written beforehand, false claimants could accuse him of compiling earlier books and cast doubt among the weak.
TABRISI:29:46-50/r9.anchor: ولقالوا: إنما تقرأ علينا ما جمعته من كتب الأولين

TABRISI:29:46-50/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:46-50/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:46-50/r10.claim: His inimitable account of earlier peoples, though he grew among people who watched him and saw no teacher, shows the Qurʾān came from God.
TABRISI:29:46-50/r10.anchor: ثم أتيت بما عجزوا عنه وجب أن يعلموا أنه من عند الله

TABRISI:29:46-50/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:46-50/r11.speaker: الشريف الأجل المرتضى
TABRISI:29:46-50/r11.claim: Al-Murtaḍā says the Prophet was not literate before prophethood; after it, either literacy or continued illiteracy is possible, and the verse does not decide.
TABRISI:29:46-50/r11.anchor: قال الشريف الأجل المرتضى علم الهدى قدس الله روحه:

TABRISI:29:46-50/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:46-50/r12.speaker: الشريف الأجل المرتضى
TABRISI:29:46-50/r12.claim: Al-Murtaḍā says the negation concerns only the time before prophethood, since prior literacy would invite suspicion; after revelation, Gabriel could have taught him.
TABRISI:29:46-50/r12.anchor: قال الشريف الأجل المرتضى علم الهدى قدس الله روحه:

FARRA:v2p317/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p317/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p317/r11.claim: Before the Qur’an, Muhammad had neither recited a book nor written with his right hand; otherwise the falsifiers, identified as Christians who knew his description, would have doubted.
FARRA:v2p317/r11.anchor: يعني النصارى الذين وجدوا صفته ويكون (لارتاب المبطلون)

FARRA:v2p317/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p317/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p317/r12.claim: Alternatively, this would have given stronger grounds for suspicion among liars in Mecca and elsewhere.
FARRA:v2p317/r12.anchor: ويكون (لارتاب المبطلون) أي لكان أشد لريبة من كذب من أهل مكة وغيرهم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#6/r1.claim: Their scriptures establish that Muhammad was unlettered; had he written, those who deny would have doubted the revelation.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#6/r1.anchor: هم يجدونك أميا في كتبهم فلو كنت تكتب لارتابوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r1.claim: Before revelation the Prophet neither read scripture nor wrote; he does not write books with his right hand, matching his unlettered description in the Torah and Gospel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r1.anchor: أي: ما كنت تقرأ قبل القرآن كتابا، أي: ما كنت قارئا قبل الوحي ولا كاتبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the People of the Book found in their scriptures that the Prophet would neither write with his right hand nor read a book, and the verse was revealed accordingly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان أهل الكتاب يجدون في كتبهم أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- لا يخط بيمينه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads idhan conditionally: if you had read or written before, the falsifiers would have doubted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: {إذا} قال الفراء: ولو كنت تتلو {لارتاب المبطلون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the falsifiers' reaction as doubt by the unbelievers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda identify the falsifiers as Quraysh.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r6.claim: If the Prophet had read and written before revelation, people could have said he learned and copied the Quran from a book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r6.anchor: وقالوا هذا شيء تعلمه محمد وكتبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r7.claim: Muqātil identifies the falsifiers as Jewish unbelievers, who would suspect him because the Torah describes the Prophet as unlettered.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني: كفار اليهود يقول: إذا لشكوا فيك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r8.claim: The People of the Book are intended: they knew the Prophet's attributes and denied his mission only after certainty, so literacy would contradict what they knew. For Quraysh, al-Farrāʾ takes the phrase to mean their suspicion would increase.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r8.anchor: وهذا هو القول؛ لأن أهل الكتاب كانوا يعرفون النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- بنعته وصفته حقا يقينا، وإنما يجحدون نبوته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r9.claim: For those already doubtful, al-Farrāʾ explains lartāba as increased suspicion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r9.anchor: ووجهه ما قال الفراء: أي: لكان أشد لريبة من كذب من أهل الكتاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r10.claim: A mubṭil is someone who lies or claims something other than the truth; anyone claiming a religion other than Islam is a falsifier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p539#2/r10.anchor: يقال: أبطل فلان: إذا كذب وادعى غير الحق

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r5.claim: “You did not recite” means “you did not read.”

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r7.claim: Had Muhammad read and written before the revelation, those who opposed the truth would have doubted it.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r8.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r8.claim: Mujahid identifies the opponents who would doubt as Quraysh polytheists.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r8.anchor: والمبطلون في تفسير مجاهد مشركو قريش.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r9.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r9.claim: Another interpretation identifies them as the People of the Book who did not believe.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم: من لم يؤمن من أهل الكتاب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r10.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r10.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the opponents as deniers, namely the Jews.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p634/r10.anchor: وفي تفسير السدي: {المبطلون} [العنكبوت: 48] يقول: المكذبون، وهم اليهود.

MAJAZ:v2p116/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p116/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p116/r1.claim: The verse means the Prophet had read no book before the Qurʾan came; min is extra, as in 69:47, and the phrase ‘nor write it with your right hand’ means write no book.
MAJAZ:v2p116/r1.anchor: ما كنت تقرأ من قبل القرآن حتى أنزل إليك ولا قبل ذلك من كتاب

MAJAZ:v2p116/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p116/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p116/r2.claim: The clause is compressed with an omitted pronoun: ‘If you had read the book and written it, the falsifiers would have doubted.’
MAJAZ:v2p116/r2.anchor: ولا تخطه بيمينك» أي ولا تكتب كتابا، ومجازه مجاز المختصر الذي فيه ضمير كقولك: ولو كنت تقرأ الكتاب وتخطه لارتاب المبطلون

ELMALILI:29:48-51/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:29:48-51/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:29:48-51/r1.claim: Muhammad had not read scripture before the Quran was revealed and still did not write, so opponents lacked a plausible human-source pretext.

ELMALILI:29:48-51/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:29:48-51/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:29:48-51/r2.claim: The falsifiers are unjust disbelievers pursuing falsehood or seeking a pretext to invalidate the message; fair-minded seekers would not doubt.
ELMALILI:29:48-51/r2.anchor: o mubtıller, yani bâtıl peşinde giden, yahut ibtâle bahane arayan

ELMALILI:29:48-51/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:29:48-51/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:29:48-51/r3.claim: Illiteracy is not a condition for miraculous eloquence, since other prophets were literate; it merely removes an excuse for hostile doubters.
ELMALILI:29:48-51/r3.anchor: Çünkü i‘câz için ümmîlik şart değildir. Nitekim sâir peygamberler ümmî değillerdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r1.claim: Reading and writing are the two basic ways to learn from another person; the verse says the Prophet did not learn from someone in either way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r1.anchor: Okumak ve yazmak, birinden öğrenim görmenin en temel iki yoludur. Âyette Hz. Peygamber’in başka birinden bu şekilde öğrenim görmediği belirtilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r2.claim: If the Prophet had been literate, Qur'an deniers could have claimed that he learned it from another person, such as a member of the People of the Book.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r2.anchor: onun okuması yazması olsaydı o zaman Kur’an’ı inkâr etmek için bahane arayanlar, onu başka birinden, meselâ bir Ehl-i kitap mensubundan okuyup yazdığını ileri sürebilirlerdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r3.claim: Such allegations were still made but failed; one important reason was the Prophet's illiteracy during the 13-year Meccan part of his 23-year prophethood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r3.anchor: Nitekim yine de bu tür iddialar gündeme getirilmiş fakat etkili olamamıştır.
