Bunun önemli sebeplerinden biri, bu ve benzeri âyetlerde ifade buyurulduğu üzere, Resûlullah’ın –en azından yirmi üç yıllık peygamberlik süresinin on üç yılını oluşturan Mekke döneminde– okuma yazmasının olmaması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:48/r4.claim: The author connects the Prophet's being unlettered to al-Aʿrāf 7:157–158.

BAQILLANI:v1p34/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p34/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p34/r1.claim: The Prophet was unlettered and had no contact with historians or prior scriptures, yet the Qur'an recounts history from Adam through earlier prophets and rulers; this knowledge therefore came by revelation.
BAQILLANI:v1p34/r1.anchor: ونحن نعلم ضرورة أن هذا مما لا سبيل إليه إلا عن تعلم وإذ كان معروفا أنه لم يكن ملابسا لأهل الآثار وحملة الأخبار

BURHAN:v3p214/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p214/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p214/r2.claim: In 29:48, لو is understood: if the Prophet had read or written before revelation, the falsifiers would have doubted.
BURHAN:v3p214/r2.anchor: معناه لو كان كذلك لارتاب المبطلون

BURHAN:v1p176/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p176/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p176/r1.claim: The count of the opening letters signals that the Prophet had not practiced writing or learned its craft, as the verse says.
BURHAN:v1p176/r1.anchor: التنبيه على أن تعداد هذه الحروف ممن لم يمارس الخط ولم يعان الطريقة

BURHAN:v1p176/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p176/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p176/r2.claim: The fourteen opening letters are half the alphabet if it has twenty-eight letters; the author instead holds that there are twenty-nine and لا has two letters.
BURHAN:v1p176/r2.anchor: انحصارها فى نصف اسماء حروف المعجم

BURHAN:v1p176/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p176/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p176/r3.claim: The alphabet's initial name alif is the name of hamza: alif itself cannot begin with a vowel, so lam provides its spoken name and its written form resembles alif.
BURHAN:v1p176/r3.anchor: فإن قلت فقد تقدم اسم الألف فى أول حروف الهجاء قلت ذلك اسم الهمزة لوجهين

BURHAN:v1p176/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p176/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p176/r4.claim: Because a letter cannot be divided in half, one letter is necessarily omitted, with omission chosen as the more concise course.
BURHAN:v1p176/r4.anchor: المذهب أن الحرف لا يمكن تنصيفه فيتعين سقوط حرف لأنه الأليق بالإيجاز

BURHAN:v1p176/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p176/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p176/r5.claim: The disjoint letters occur in twenty-nine surahs, matching the alphabet's twenty-nine letters; their shapes were not matched because some are heavy to pronounce.
BURHAN:v1p176/r5.anchor: مجيئها فى تسع وعشرين سورة بعدد الحروف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:45-48/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:45-48/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:45-48/r6.claim: Muhammad had not read or written a book before the Qur’an; otherwise opponents could doubt him and accuse him of composing it from a book.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:45-48/r6.anchor: من كتاب ولا تخطه } ولا تكتبه { بيمينك إذا لارتاب المبطلون } لشكوا فيك واتهموك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:45-48/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:45-48/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:45-48/r7.claim: The “people of falsehood” here are the unbelievers of Quraysh.

BURHAN:v4p372/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p372/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p372/r3.claim: The text also illustrates reconstructing a conditional answer: if God had other gods, each would take its creation; if the Prophet had read or written earlier, deniers would have doubted.

ITQAN:v4p328/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p328/r3.speaker: البارزي
ITQAN:v4p328/r3.claim: Al-Barizi says تتلو is better than تقرأ because the latter is heavier with its hamza.
ITQAN:v4p328/r3.anchor: ﴿ وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ﴾ أحسن من التعبير ب ( تقرأ ) لثقله بالهمزة

JISHUMI:v8p5576/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5576/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5576/r12.claim: Khaṭṭ means writing: the verb khaṭṭa-yakhuṭṭu means to write; the source also gives the command and prohibition forms.
JISHUMI:v8p5576/r12.anchor: الخط: معروف، [خط] يخط: كتب، والأمر خط، والنهي لا تخط

JISHUMI:v8p5576/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5576/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5576/r13.claim: Rib and irtiyāb mean doubt accompanied by suspicion.
JISHUMI:v8p5576/r13.anchor: والارتياب والريب: شك مع تهمة، رابني هذا الأمر
